findings.back_translation: Hides with the absence of a store page
findings.issue: Ungrammatical and unclear filter chip; a user cannot tell that games without a store page are being hidden. Sibling chips use 'Ainult ilma poelehata' / 'Kaasa arvatud ...' patterns.
Brand should take the genitive in this construction; the translation elsewhere already inflects it (GameLibi, GameLibist).
Uses 'installima', but nearly every other row uses 'paigaldama' for install.

findings.en: This game's macOS build is 32-bit only and cannot run on this version of macOS. GameLib can reinstall it through CrossOver instead, which will redownload the Windows version.
findings.tr: Selle mängu macOS versioon on ainult 32-bitine ega tööta selle macOS versiooniga. GameLib saab selle asemel uuesti paigaldada CrossOver kaudu, mis laadib alla Windowsi versiooni.
findings.back_translation: This game's macOS version is only 32-bit and does not work with this macOS version. GameLib can instead reinstall via CrossOver, which downloads the Windows version.
findings.issue: Estonian orthography needs the hyphenated genitive 'macOS-i versioon'. 'Re-' of redownload is dropped, a small nuance loss.
findings.suggested: Selle mängu macOS-i versioon on ainult 32-bitine ega tööta selle macOS-i versiooniga. GameLib saab selle asemel CrossOveri kaudu uuesti paigaldada, mis laadib Windowsi versiooni uuesti alla.

findings.en: SteamGridDB artwork search is unavailable on this build.
findings.tr: SteamGridDB kujunduse otsing pole selle versiooniga saadaval.
findings.back_translation: SteamGridDB design search is not available with this version.
findings.issue: 'kujundus' (design/layout) is an odd rendering of game artwork; 'pildid' / 'pildimaterjal' fits better. 'selle versiooniga' and 'selles versioonis' are mixed across rows (same for steamgriddb.error.unavailable and settings.steamgriddb.*).
findings.suggested: SteamGridDB piltide otsing pole selles versioonis saadaval.

findings.en: This reveals the key — removing it from Giftable spares for good — and redeems it on your Steam account. There's no undo.
findings.tr: See paljastab võtme — eemaldades selle jäädavalt kinkimiseks sobivate hulgast — ja lunastab selle sinu Steami kontol. Seda ei saa tagasi võtta.
findings.back_translation: This exposes the key, permanently removing it from among those suitable for gifting, and redeems it on your Steam account. It cannot be undone.
findings.issue: 'Giftable spares' is a named UI section rendered elsewhere as 'Kingitavad varuvõtmed'. Here it is paraphrased, so the user cannot match it to the section. 'paljastama' (expose/unmask) is also a heavy word for revealing a key.
findings.suggested: See avab võtme — eemaldades selle jäädavalt Kingitavatest varuvõtmetest — ja lunastab selle sinu Steami kontol. Seda ei saa tagasi võtta.

findings.en: You already own this on Steam
findings.tr: Sul on see juba Steam'is olemas
findings.back_translation: You already have this on Steam
findings.issue: Estonian does not use an apostrophe when a word ends in a pronounced consonant, so it should be 'Steamis'. Other rows correctly write 'Steamis' and 'Steami', so this is also inconsistent.
findings.suggested: Sul on see juba Steamis olemas

findings.en: You already own this on Steam — activation will likely fail there.
findings.tr: Sul on see juba Steam'is olemas — aktiveerimine seal tõenäoliselt ebaõnnestub.
findings.back_translation: You already have this on Steam — activation there will probably fail.
findings.issue: Same unneeded apostrophe as c2Title ('Steam'is' should be 'Steamis').
findings.suggested: Sul on see juba Steamis olemas — aktiveerimine seal tõenäoliselt ebaõnnestub.

findings.issue: Unneeded apostrophe ('Steamis').
Unneeded apostrophe ('Steamis'). Word order also reads better as 'Steamis olemas'.
'nõudma' means demand or require, which is the wrong sense for claiming a key in UI. Other rows use 'lunastama' for claiming.

findings.en: Anyone with this link can claim the key — once redeemed, it's gone for good. You'll finish gifting it on Humble's own site.
findings.tr: Igaüks, kellel on see link, saab võtme endale nõuda — kui see on kasutatud, on see jäädavalt läinud. Kingi lõpuleviimine toimub Humble enda saidil.
findings.back_translation: Anyone who has this link can demand the key for themselves — once used, it's gone forever. Completion of the gift happens on Humble's own site.
findings.issue: The brand needs the genitive ('Humble'i enda saidil'). 'Kingituse' reads more naturally than 'Kingi'. 'nõudma' has the same demand sense problem as claimWizardTitle.
findings.suggested: Igaüks, kellel on see link, saab võtme endale võtta — kui see on kasutatud, on see jäädavalt läinud. Kingituse viid lõpule Humble'i enda saidil.

findings.issue: 'Humble's' looks like an English possessive. The Estonian inessive of Humble (pronounced ending in /l/) is 'Humble'is'.
The ellipsis was dropped. Other progress strings keep it.

'Redeem' is translated three ways across the file: kasutama (here, markRedeemed, redeemedAnnotation), lunastama (state.redeemed, redeemSteamKey.title), and aktiveerima (redeemSteamKey.redeem, redeemKey.*). Pick one; 'lunastama' is the most natural.
This doesn't match the state label 'Lunastatud' that the action produces.

findings.back_translation: We could not confirm it finished — syncing checks it

findings.suggested: Me ei suutnud kinnitada, et see lõpule jõudis — sünkrooni, et kontrollida

The instruction became a statement, so the user is not told to act.
This is the same word used for Cancel (box.cancel, activateDismiss). Estonian UI convention for Undo is 'Võta tagasi'.

As a status label, the participle 'Ebaõnnestunud' is more natural than the finite past verb.

terminology_notes: Install = 'paigaldama' is dominant and correct, but 'installima/installid' leaks into three rows. Library = 'teek' is consistent except for one 'varamu' in sideload.import-hint.content. Redeem is split three ways (kasutama / lunastama / aktiveerima), and 'Aktiveeri' is shared by both Activate and Redeem; recommend Redeem = lunastama and Activate = aktiveerima. Reveal is split between 'paljastama' (actions and annotations) and 'avama' (state labels); pick one, preferably 'avama'. Undo is rendered 'Tühista', the same word as Cancel; use 'Võta tagasi'. Sync is split between 'sünkroonima' (Humble) and colloquial 'sünkima' (Steam). 'Giftable spares' is a named section ('Kingitavad varuvõtmed') but is paraphrased in one row. Bottle = 'pudel', except one English 'bottle'i'. Register is informal 'sina' throughout, except about 5 formal 'teie' rows. Brand inflection is mostly right (Steami, Steamis, GameLibist, Humble Bundle'isse), but a few rows add an unneeded apostrophe (Steam'is, GameLib'is) or a wrong one (Humble's), or omit the hyphen on the macOS genitive.
overall:
The Estonian translation is good overall. Meanings are accurately preserved, all {{placeholders}}, the
/<3> tags and the " entities are intact, brands are never translated, and there are no critical errors. The one major issue is an ungrammatical filter chip (chipNoStorePageHidden). The remaining findings are consistency problems (redeem, reveal, undo and sync terms, formal vs informal address) and small orthography issues with inflected brands. Confidence limits: I judged the placeholder-inflection cases (syncError's '{{time}} eest', diskSpaceFreeOfTotal's '{{total}}-st') without knowing the runtime placeholder values, and my Estonian register judgments come from a non-native reviewer, so a native speaker should confirm the minor stylistic calls.
